findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add named tests exercising the two RETURN-shaped soft-error paths: assert explain_criterion emits criterion_unknown_id/criterion_registry_malformed/criterion_missing_file (mapped from kind) while KEEPING kind, and _mcp_llm emits llm_unavailable while KEEPING resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic.
evidence: Per-code pinning (AC4): 'for each emitted code (ticket_not_found, concurrency_conflict, claim_failed, plus command_failed fallback)' — the return-shaped codes are absent from this list
Design step 3(b) introduces criterion_unknown_id/criterion_registry_malformed/criterion_missing_file and llm_unavailable and asserts fields are 'PRESERVED, not dropped', but no test names these paths
AC6 requires the preserved-fields property be verified, yet no test exercises the explain_criterion / _mcp_llm return-shaped error surface
findings.finding: The plan adds vocabulary codes to the two RETURN-shaped soft-error paths (_mcp_reads.py:77 explain_criterion mapping exc.kind to criterion_unknown_id/criterion_registry_malformed/criterion_missing_file, and _mcp_llm.py:31 setting error to llm_unavailable) but the test plan's per-code pinning enumerates only ticket_not_found, concurrency_conflict, claim_failed, and command_failed — none of these newly-migrated return-shaped codes are named in any test, so the migration of the two ad-hoc shapes could ship without a test proving each emits its vocabulary code while preserving kind/resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic.
findings.location: Test plan (held-out oracle); AC6 (Every MCP error... carries an error code... fields PRESERVED)
scenarios: The explain_criterion migration silently drops the kind field (or emits a code outside KNOWN_ERROR_CODES) and no test catches it
The _mcp_llm migration overwrites error but loses resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic, closing green because no test observes the return-shaped soft-error shape
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the per-code pinning and preservation tests to cover the return-shaped codes: for each kind assert both the vocabulary error code (a KNOWN_ERROR_CODES member) and the retained companion field(s).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly whether every resolution_class value maps to the single code llm_unavailable, or enumerate the additional per-class codes and add them to KNOWN_ERROR_CODES.
evidence: 'sets error to a vocabulary code (e.g. llm_unavailable derived from its resolution_class)'
KNOWN_ERROR_CODES lists only 'llm_unavailable' among LLM-related codes
findings.finding: Step 3(b) says the _mcp_llm.py error code is 'e.g. llm_unavailable derived from its resolution_class', implying a mapping from resolution_class values to codes, but KNOWN_ERROR_CODES lists only the single LLM code llm_unavailable — leaving unstated whether all resolution_class values collapse to llm_unavailable or whether additional per-class codes are intended.
scenarios: Executor implementing _mcp_llm.py migration must decide whether each resolution_class maps to a distinct code (none of which are in KNOWN_ERROR_CODES) or all map to llm_unavailable.
findings.suggested_fix: State that all LLM resolution_class values map to the single vocabulary code llm_unavailable (the only LLM member of KNOWN_ERROR_CODES), with resolution_class preserved as an additional discriminating field.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the _mcp_llm.py error-code derivation: either state the return-path emits the constant `llm_unavailable` in `error` (branch signal preserved in the PRESERVED resolution_class/retryable fields), or enumerate the per-resolution_class codes explicitly in KNOWN_ERROR_CODES so the vocabulary-closure test (AC2) holds.
evidence: ResolutionClass is a closed 8-class enum with no 'unavailable' member (src/rebar/llm/failure.py:37-48)
KNOWN_ERROR_CODES enumerated in Design item 1 lists only 'llm_unavailable' for the LLM path; the classifier maps 'isinstance(exc, LLMError) -> llm_unavailable' (a single code)
Plan text: 'derived from its resolution_class' vs the single-code closure — the two cannot both hold unless the derivation is a constant
findings.finding: The _mcp_llm.py return-path design is internally inconsistent: it says the error code is 'derived from its resolution_class', but resolution_class is a closed 8-value enum (WAIT_AND_RETRY, RETRY_NOW, INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS, CHANGE_SETTINGS, CHANGE_INPUT, CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL, FIX_AGENT_DESIGN, NEEDS_INVESTIGATION) while KNOWN_ERROR_CODES lists only the single code llm_unavailable for this path. Either the derivation collapses all 8 classes to llm_unavailable (making 'derived from resolution_class' misleading) or it produces per-class codes absent from KNOWN_ERROR_CODES (violating the vocabulary-closure AC2 the plan asserts).
findings.location: Design section item 3(b): '_mcp_llm.py:31 sets error to a vocabulary code (e.g. llm_unavailable derived from its resolution_class)'
scenarios: An LLM failure whose resolution_class is CHANGE_INPUT or NEEDS_INVESTIGATION: implementer must pick a code for `error`
Vocabulary-closure test (AC2) asserting MCP can only emit KNOWN_ERROR_CODES members
findings.suggested_fix: Set `error` to the constant `llm_unavailable` for the LLMError return-path (matching the classifier's single LLMError->llm_unavailable mapping), and keep resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic as the preserved branch signal — drop the 'derived from resolution_class' phrasing, since the discriminator is intentionally coarse and the fine-grained signal lives in the preserved fields.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the explicit ResolutionClass(8 values)->error-code mapping for _mcp_llm failures, add every resulting code to KNOWN_ERROR_CODES, and specify the code used when outcome_of(exc) returns None (resolution_class absent).
evidence: Plan: '_mcp_llm.py:31 sets error to a vocabulary code (e.g. llm_unavailable derived from its resolution_class)'
KNOWN_ERROR_CODES lists exactly one LLM code: 'llm_unavailable' — no per-class codes

rebar/llm/failure.py:37-48 — ResolutionClass is a closed 8-class enum: WAIT_AND_RETRY, RETRY_NOW, INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS, CHANGE_SETTINGS, CHANGE_INPUT, CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL, FIX_AGENT_DESIGN, NEEDS_INVESTIGATION
_mcp_llm.py:29-34 — outcome_of(exc) may return None, so resolution_class is None on that branch, leaving 'derived from resolution_class' undefined

AC6/AC (section 3) require 'the existing agent-branching fields (resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic) are PRESERVED' — but if all 8 classes collapse to llm_unavailable the code adds no discriminator beyond the preserved fields; if they DON'T collapse, the extra codes are missing from KNOWN_ERROR_CODES and would violate AC2 vocabulary closure
findings.finding: The MCP LLM failure path maps an 8-value closed enum (ResolutionClass) to error codes without defining the mapping, and the None-outcome fallback is unspecified.
findings.location: Design section 3(b) '_mcp_llm.py:31 sets error to a vocabulary code (e.g. llm_unavailable derived from its resolution_class)'; KNOWN_ERROR_CODES enumeration in Design section 1
scenarios: An LLM tool fails with resolution_class=WAIT_AND_RETRY vs CHANGE_INPUT — executor must decide whether both emit error=llm_unavailable or distinct codes
An LLMError for which outcome_of() returns None — executor has no resolution_class to derive a code from
findings.suggested_fix: State that ALL ResolutionClass values (and the None-outcome case) map to the single code llm_unavailable, with the 8-way disposition preserved only in the retained resolution_class/retryable fields; OR enumerate one code per class and add each to KNOWN_ERROR_CODES.

findings.finding: The _mcp_llm.py soft-error migration derives the vocabulary `error` code from `resolution_class`, but `resolution_class` is a closed 8-member enum (WAIT_AND_RETRY, RETRY_NOW, INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS, CHANGE_SETTINGS, CHANGE_INPUT, CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL, FIX_AGENT_DESIGN, NEEDS_INVESTIGATION) while KNOWN_ERROR_CODES contains exactly one llm code (`llm_unavailable`); the mapping from the 8 classes to vocabulary code(s) is never defined, so an executor cannot deterministically produce a KNOWN_ERROR_CODES member for a returned LLM failure.
findings.location: Design step 3(b) ('llm_unavailable derived from its resolution_class') + KNOWN_ERROR_CODES list in Design step 1
findings.suggested_fix: State that every LLM return-failure maps to the single code `llm_unavailable` regardless of resolution_class (which is preserved as the richer branching field), so `error` stays a KNOWN_ERROR_CODES member while resolution_class carries the 8-way disposition.

findings.finding: The vocabulary-closure test (AC2) requires every literal passed to error_envelope(...) across src/rebar/ to be a member of KNOWN_ERROR_CODES, but two census entries do not state the actual literal: next_batch.py:536 is described only as '(next-batch reader code)' and field_reads.py:88 as '(field reader code)'. The plan asserts KNOWN_ERROR_CODES contains `next_batch_failed` and `field_read_failed`, but does not confirm those are the literals actually emitted at those sites. If the real literals differ, the closure test fails.
findings.location: CLI emitter census + Design step 1 (KNOWN_ERROR_CODES frozenset)
findings.suggested_fix: Read the two call sites, quote the exact string arguments, and either confirm they equal the listed members or list the true literals in KNOWN_ERROR_CODES.

findings.finding: The plan lists `next_batch_failed` and `field_read_failed` in KNOWN_ERROR_CODES and presents them in the census as the 'next-batch reader code' / 'field reader code', but next_batch.py:536 and field_reads.py:88 both emit the literal `ticket_not_found`, not any distinct code.
findings.location: Design step 1 (KNOWN_ERROR_CODES members) and 'Complete CLI emitter census' (next_batch.py:536 / field_reads.py:88)
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the two reader sites' literals; if they stay `ticket_not_found`, remove `next_batch_failed`/`field_read_failed` from KNOWN_ERROR_CODES and the census, or explicitly scope retargeting those sites to the new codes as part of this ticket.

findings.finding: The classifier maps `ConcurrencyError -> concurrency_conflict`, but the actual concurrency claim failure raises `ConcurrencyMismatch`, defined as a subclass of `CommandError` (not `ConcurrencyError`) and raised without an error_code, so error_code_for would classify it via the error_code/fallback branch (command_failed), not concurrency_conflict.
findings.location: Design step 1 (classifier mapping 'ConcurrencyError -> concurrency_conflict') and Test plan cross-interface AC5 'concurrency mismatch'
findings.suggested_fix: Add `isinstance(exc, ConcurrencyMismatch) -> concurrency_conflict` to error_code_for (importing the type from _commands.txn), or have txn.py raise ConcurrencyMismatch with error_code='concurrency_conflict' so the error_code branch classifies it.

findings.finding: The MCP tool-body guard builds the envelope via exc.message, but the guard's own named targets RebarError/ConcurrencyError/TrackerRootError do not expose a .message attribute (src/rebar/_errors.py only calls super().__init__(message), unlike ReadError and CommandError which set self.message). exc.message on a plain ConcurrencyError/TrackerRootError would raise AttributeError inside the guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Use str(exc) for the message, or add self.message = message to RebarError.__init__ so all guard targets expose it uniformly.

findings.finding: The plan retargets the deps reader classification at reads_cli.py:411 to isinstance(TicketNotFoundError) and raises TicketNotFoundError at reads.py:469, but reads.py:469's message is "ticket '<id>' does not exist" (not 'not found'). Today reads_cli.py:410 keys on "'not found' in exc.message", so a genuinely-missing ticket on deps currently emits code `deps_failed`, not `ticket_not_found`. The isinstance retarget would flip that emitted code, changing CLI envelope output and contradicting AC6's byte-identical claim.
findings.location: Files (impact): 'reads.py:310/313/469 ... CLI/classifier switch to isinstance (output unchanged)'

findings.finding: The MCP guard's envelope formula uses `exc.message` unconditionally, but RebarError/ConcurrencyError/TrackerRootError and LLMError — classes the guard explicitly catches — do not set a `.message` attribute (RebarError.__init__ sets only returncode/stderr; LLMError adds nothing to RuntimeError). The guard will raise AttributeError instead of producing an envelope for exactly the concurrency_conflict path AC5 tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the guard's message argument from `exc.message` to a fallback such as `getattr(exc, "message", "") or str(exc)`, or add/normalize a `.message` on RebarError and LLMError; add a guard unit test covering ConcurrencyError to pin that concurrency_conflict envelopes build without AttributeError.
